SB 1383 SHORT-LIVED CLIMATE POLLUTANT REDUCTION ACT
Senate Bill (SB) 1383 is a statewide effort to reduce emissions of short-lived climate pollutants,
like methane gas. If organic materials (such as paper, cardboard, food scraps, food-soiled paper
and yard trimmings) are left to decompose in a landfill, the decomposition will emit methane, a
powerful super-pollutant which contributes to climate change.
What does SB 1383 mean for
businesses?
Recycling and organics recycling services have been
required for a number of years via Assembly Bill (AB)
341 and AB 1826, as well as Stockton Municipal
Code. Under statewide SB 1383 regulations, there
are specific and detailed requirements for all cities,
businesses and residents. Read below and on the
reverse side to learn more about the requirements
for businesses.
Mandatory Recycling
All businesses are required to have recycling and organics
recycling collection services no matter how much trash is
generated by the business.
SUBSCRIBE TO RECYCLING AND ORGANICS
RECYCLING SERVICE WITH YOUR GARBAGE
SERVICE PROVIDER. CONTACT REPUBLIC
SERVICES OR WASTE MANAGEMENT FOR
ASSISTANCE TODAY.
A landscape or gardening service that hauls organic materials away from the business is required to
discard materials at City-approved facilities only. Recordkeeping requirements must be followed.
Contact our hotline at 209-937-8831, if you do not understand these requirements.
BUSINESSES MUST PROVIDE CONTAINERS FOR ORGANIC WASTE AND RECYCLABLES
IN ALL AREAS WHERE DISPOSAL CONTAINERS ARE PROVIDED TO CUSTOMERS
(EXCEPT RESTROOMS)
If a business does not generate any of the materials that
would be collected in a specific container for its
customers, then it does not have to provide that
container.
Recycling and organic collection containers must be of

the required color: blue for recycling and green for
organics. Otherwise, the containers must have have the
required labeling for sorting waste.
Containers purchased prior to January 1, 2022 that do
not comply with the color or label requirements do not
need to be replaced unless they are no longer functional
or until January 1, 2036, whichever occurs first.
